stem: The graph of the linear function \(h\) is shown in the \(xy\)-plane. Which of the following is the solution set of the inequality \(h(x) \le -3\)?
solution: The line passes through \((0, 6)\) and \((4, 0)\): slope \(\frac{0 - 6}{4 - 0} = -\frac{3}{2}\), so \(h(x) = -\frac{3}{2}x + 6\).
Divide by \(-\frac{3}{2}\) and reverse the sign: \(x \ge 6\). The line is at or below \(y = -3\) from \(x = 6\) onward.

explanation.A: Incorrect. Dividing by the negative slope reverses the inequality sign; the line falls, so it is below \(-3\) to the right of 6, not the left.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This solves \(-\frac{3}{2}x \le -3\), forgetting to subtract the \(y\)-intercept 6 first.
explanation.C: Incorrect. \(x = 4\) is where \(h(x) = 0\), the \(x\)-intercept, not where \(h(x) = -3\).

verify:
P = lambda s: value(s.replace('\\le', '<=').replace('\\ge', '>='))
x = symbols('x')
h = sympify(figure['curves'][0]['expr'])
s = solve_univariate_inequality(h <= -3, x, relational=False)
assert s == Interval(6, oo)
assert solve_univariate_inequality(P(choices[answer]), x, relational=False) == s
assert all(solve_univariate_inequality(P(choices[k]), x, relational=False) != s for k in choices if k != answer)
